verdict.rationale: Recurly documents its own usage-based billing: consumption-driven add-ons whose measured units are tracked and charged at the end of each billing cycle. That implies usage gets recorded, but nothing describes a high-volume event ingestion pipeline. The pack never mentions streaming or ingesting usage events, idempotency keys or deduplication, backdated or late-arriving usage timestamps, or throughput limits. Missing for 10: a documented usage-event ingestion API, high-volume or streaming ingestion, idempotent ingestion, backdating support, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream high-volume usage events — API calls, tokens, compute-seconds — into a metering pipeline with idempotent ingestion and backdating support

citations.quote: Usage-based billing lets you define consumption-driven add-ons, track measured units across plans, and charge at the end of every billing cycle
Measured units describe the usage tracked by a usage-based add-on and enable consistent reporting across multiple add-ons and plans.
